q-42918.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -18 & -13 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
q-42918.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{34}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -18 & -13 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-3{R}_{3}.$

A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
q-91188.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{31}=3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-{C}_{1}.$
